subject: Private deployment: NetOps / SecOps clarifications and next owners
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
To: Brynn Holt <brynn.holt@clearingbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: NetOps / SecOps clarifications and next owners

Hi Brynn — great to meet today. Quick recap from my side plus a short list of items we need to lock to progress a Private VPC deployment: we captured these on the call but wanted to make them explicit so NetOps / SecOps can align.

Summary of call: ClearingBank is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (PrivateLink or VPC Peering) instead of Hosted API — primary drivers are data residency and strict egress controls. Next step is a focused NetOps and SecOps deep-dive to confirm connectivity pattern and ownership.

Outstanding technical asks (what we need from ClearingBank):
- Decision preference: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering (and any constraints that would force one over the other).
- Egress IP allowlist: list of CIDR(s) / static IPs + whether you require a tenant-per-vpc or shared egress.
- DNS & outbound resolution: will your environment allow outbound DNS to Redwood-managed resolvers, or do you require forwarding via internal DNS?
- Proxy/NAT model: are you behind a corporate outbound proxy or do you use NAT gateway(s)? If proxy, we need host/port and auth model.
- Throughput & latency expectations: expected RPS and average sequence length per request (token counts) so we size Dedicated pools if needed.
- Compliance evidence: any additional audit artifacts we should prepare beyond SOC2 checklist.

What Redwood can provide now:
- Sample network diagram and a short requirements PDF (attached).
- A draft SOW for Private VPC onboarding (if helpful) to frame ownership and acceptance tests.
- NetOps deep-dive: propose a 60-minute session with your NetOps + our Priyom (network lead) and Marissa (solutions).

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) Brynn to share a network diagram (or ops alias with diagrams) and an initial allowance for egress IPs.
2) We schedule the NetOps deep-dive for next week; please advise times.
3) Redwood to circulate draft SOW and owner matrix.

Attachments: redwood_privatenet_requirements.pdf (attached)

Thanks — Rohan

--
Rohan Mehta
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.com
[Attachment: redwood_privatenet_requirements.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Brynn Holt <brynn.holt@clearingbank.com>

Cc: ops-team@clearingbank.com
Date: Fri, 3 Aug 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: NetOps / SecOps clarifications and next owners

Thanks Rohan — appreciate the concise recap. Attaching the diagram our NetOps team sketched during the call. A few quick clarifications from us: 

- We prefer VPC Peering for lower management overhead, but Security is asking for a PrivateLink option if we can't ASG lock down egress effectively.
- For egress allowlist: we can provide an initial /28 for testing and are open to moving to a larger block once throughput estimates are agreed.
- DNS: we use internal forwarders; we will likely require DNS forwarding rather than letting Redwood resolve externally.
- Proxy: we do not use an outbound corporate proxy for this traffic — we route via NAT gateways.

Attaching: clearingbank_network_diagram.png

We can do a NetOps session next Tue 8/8 between 10–12 PT or Wed 8/9 morning PT. Ops alias will join.

-Brynn

[Attachment: clearingbank_network_diagram.png (image/png)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Brynn Holt <brynn.holt@clearingbank.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 6 Aug 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: NetOps / SecOps clarifications and next owners

Thanks Brynn — diagram received and very helpful. I've sketched an owner matrix below to avoid confusion in the NetOps session: 

Owner matrix (proposal):
- ClearingBank NetOps: VPC routing rules, internal DNS forwarders, firewall rules for inbound peering, ASN allocation if needed.
- ClearingBank SecOps: approval for PrivateLink (if used), review of audit evidence, role-based access to logs.
- Redwood (Marissa/Priyom): provide peering endpoint configuration, list of expected source IPs for allowlist, SOW for onboarding, staging tests and acceptance criteria.
- Redwood Sales (Kimberly): procurement & SOW signature, commercial terms and Dedicated capacity sizing guidance.

Action items before the deep-dive: 
1) ClearingBank to share the initial /28 for testing and any firewall policy templates you require (Brynn).
2) Redwood to produce a draft SOW and short runbook for NetOps handoff (I'll attach sample_sow_privatenet.docx).
3) Priyom to prepare expected egress IP list and a short checklist for NAT vs. Proxy cases.

Proposed NetOps slot: Tue 8/8 10:30–11:30 PT (we'll book 60 minutes; let us know if ops needs a full 90).

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Brynn Holt <brynn.holt@clearingbank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Aug 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment: NetOps / SecOps clarifications and next owners

Hi all — a few technical notes ahead of the NetOps call so we can be efficient: 

1) IPs: for initial testing a /28 is fine. For production we typically recommend a /24 if you expect >1k concurrent connections across tenants; otherwise we can support NAT translation during the initial ramp. I'll publish the minimal port list we'll need (TCP/443 + outbound ephemeral for callbacks).

2) DNS: forwarding to an internal resolver is ok — we'll need a small set of FQDNs for health checks and to validate TLS certs during onboarding. If you require mTLS between your forwarder and our endpoint, please flag that now.

3) PrivateLink vs Peering tradeoffs (short):
- Peering: simpler, lower latency, but you need to manage route table entries and potential overlapping CIDRs.
- PrivateLink: more control over access (service endpoints) and easier multi-tenant segmentation, but requires ENI attachments and slightly more setup on our side.

4) Throughput question: Brynn — can you share expected peak RPS and average prompt token length for the first pilot? That drives whether we recommend Dedicated capacity aside from the connectivity mode.

I'll attach the expected egress IP list and port checklist to the NetOps invite.

--
Priyom Das
NetOps Lead, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
